question: Is a heavier padel racket associated with more upper-body injuries in amateur players?
answer: Yes, in a study of amateur padel players, a racket weight equal to or greater than 350 g was found to be related to the appearance of injuries [munoz2022 p.5]. Specifically, the appearance of injuries is greater among amateur players when using a racket weight of 350 g or more, alongside factors such as playing more than six hours a week [munoz2022 p.7]. Tendon and muscular injuries—particularly affecting the elbow and shoulder—are the most common in this population [munoz2022 p.7]. Players experiencing persistent pain or injuries should consult a physiotherapist or doctor.

In a survey of amateur padel players, 84.8% of men and 63.9% of women reported using rackets weighing 350 g or more [munoz2022 p.4].

question: How is racket shape linked to playing style and which shapes do male and female amateurs prefer?
answer:
Traditionally, racket shapes are linked to playing styles through mass distribution: diamond shapes offer a higher balance favoring power shots for attacking players, round shapes provide a lower balance for control shots suited to defensive players, and teardrop shapes occupy a polyvalent range [blanes2023 p.11-12]. 

In a survey of amateur players, shape preferences differed significantly between sexes [munoz2022 p.4, p.7]. Male amateurs tended to use more diamond-shaped rackets (35.9%), alongside teardrop (39.7%) and round (24.4%), aligning with a more aggressive style of play closer to the net [munoz2022 p.4, p.7]. In contrast, female amateurs predominantly preferred round-shaped rackets (44.2%), followed by teardrop (33.3%) and diamond (22.4%), corresponding to a more conservative game from the middle and back of the court [munoz2022 p.4, p.7].
